strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear demonstration of oscillation and outlier issues in FP4 training through convincing empirical analysis (Figures 1-2)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model sizes (70M-370M) and data scales (50B-200B tokens) with extensive ablation studies validating each component's contribution
Technically sound contributions with theoretically grounded unbiased gradient estimation design using stochastic rounding and careful tensor alignment
Valuable insights from loss decomposition analysis (Tables 5-6) revealing which quantizers and modules are most sensitive to quantization
Clear presentation with well-documented hyperparameters, effective use of visualizations, and practical algorithms with pseudocode
Novel application of oscillation suppression to LLM pre-training from scratch (prior work focused on vision transformers and QAT)
weaknesses: Limited experimental scale - maximum 370M parameters is modest for ICML 2026; experiments at 1B+ parameters are needed to validate scalability of the approach
No hardware efficiency validation despite claiming efficiency benefits - no actual speedup measurements or throughput improvements demonstrated; NVFP4 hardware unavailability limits reproducibility
Overstated claims of near-lossless training - gap to BF16 remains significant (~1.6-1.59 PPL points on WikiText-103 for 370M), indicating the method does not achieve full precision parity

Modest algorithmic novelty - most techniques are refinements of existing work (double-block quantization is straightforward NVFP4 constraint handling; RHT, stochastic rounding, Hadamard transforms from prior work; OutControl adapts inference technique LLM.int8() to training)

Insufficient theoretical justification for critical design choices: weight reset to bin centers for oscillation suppression lacks formal optimality analysis; RHT's harm to forward pass explained qualitatively not quantitatively; static outlier selection's consistency through training not rigorously justified

Hyperparameter sensitivity underexplored - oscillation threshold τ_osci=8 appears critical but no sensitivity analysis provided; outlier percentages vary across models without principled justification
Statistical rigor concerns - no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; unclear if performance differences are statistically significant

FP6×FP4 results (Figure 7) undermine the FP4×FP4 contribution - substantial improvements achieved by just switching precision, raising questions about the relative contribution of proposed methods vs. higher precision
Code availability not mentioned; limited reproducibility due to NVFP4 hardware requirements restricted to Blackwell GPUs

Fairness of baseline comparisons questionable - unclear if baselines received equal hyperparameter tuning effort; NVIDIA's method intentionally uses mixed precision, making direct comparison potentially unfair

strengths: Clear problem motivation with compelling empirical evidence for weight oscillation and outlier issues (Figures 1-3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple model sizes, extensive downstream tasks, and thorough ablation studies
Technically sound mathematical formulations for quantization, unbiased gradient estimation, and algorithmic components
Consistent improvements across all tested configurations showing practical benefits of combined approach
Good reproducibility effort with detailed hyperparameters and open-source codebase (OLMo)
weaknesses: Critical limitation: Complete absence of actual speedup measurements—paper cannot validate its core efficiency claim despite 'unavailability of hardware that supports low-precision NVFP4 computations,' making practical impact impossible to assess
Severely limited experimental scale (maximum 370M parameters, 200B tokens) insufficient to generalize to modern LLM training; behavior at billion-parameter scales unclear

Limited algorithmic novelty: OsciReset is weight-resetting to bin centers (intuitive but simple with no theoretical justification); OutControl extends LLM.int8(); relies heavily on known techniques (stochastic rounding, Hadamard transforms)
Questionable outlier selection design: static selection claims based on visual evidence from only 3 samples (Figure 3) without quantitative consistency analysis or ablation on 5%/10% ratios
OsciReset lacks theoretical justification—why bin-center resetting is optimal vs. alternative stabilization methods unexplored; mechanism of improvement on global optimization unclear
Unfair baseline comparison: NVIDIA's mixed-precision baseline (BF16 some blocks) vs. fully-FP4 TetraJet-v2; TetraJet-v2-base alone shows only ~0.7-0.9 PPL improvement
Precision switching results (Figure 7) showing superior FP6×FP4 performance contradicts main narrative of fully-FP4 training, undermining stated goal
Many hyperparameters (τ_osci, Tstart, Tperiod, outlier ratio) with model-dependent values contradict claim of 'little tuning'; no sensitivity analysis provided
Limited robustness: single dataset (OLMo-2-Mix-1124), no evaluation on coding/reasoning tasks, downstream evaluation only for 370M model
Statistical rigor concerns: no error bars, confidence intervals, or clear specification of averaging procedures; potentially single-run results

strengths: Novel systematic identification and treatment of weight oscillation phenomenon in LLM training (first for LLMs), with well-visualized empirical demonstration and effective OsciReset solution
Technically sound double-block quantization approach addressing NVFP4 numerical constraints with clear superiority over NVIDIA's baseline shown in ablations

Strong and consistent empirical results: 51.3% reduction in performance gap to BF16 across multiple model sizes (70M-370M) and data scales (50B-200B tokens) with comprehensive downstream task evaluation
Unbiased gradient framework carefully designed with deterministic forward/stochastic backward rounding, properly aligned to ensure theoretical convergence properties

Comprehensive experimental analysis including thorough ablations (Table 3), loss decomposition revealing quantization sensitivity patterns (Tables 5-6), and comparison of oscillation suppression methods (Figure 5)
Useful practical insights for future work including identification that forward pass and MLP.ffn2 are most quantization-sensitive, and FP6×FP4 offers substantial improvement
Clear presentation with well-specified algorithms, informative visualizations of oscillation phenomenon and outlier patterns, and detailed hyperparameter tables enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: No validation on actual NVFP4 hardware due to unavailability - claimed efficiency gains remain unvalidated; software simulation may not capture actual kernel performance, memory bandwidth effects, or hardware scheduling

Limited experimental scale: 370M parameters and 200B tokens vs. billions-scale modern LLM training; scalability to 7B-70B models remains uncertain and some quantization behaviors may only emerge at larger scales

Theoretical gaps: oscillation suppression mechanism explained empirically rather than theoretically with no convergence guarantees; convergence claim relies on citation without formal proof for NVFP4+double-block case; hyperparameter τ_osci=8 appears arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis

OutControl design partially unjustified: static outlier selection potentially suboptimal but optimality loss not quantified; 10% outlier ratio appears arbitrary with no ablation on this percentage; different inputs may have varying patterns not captured

Unexplained interaction effects: Table 5 shows individual gradient quantizations have minimal impact but combined they give +0.21 PPL change; mechanistic explanation lacking, suggesting possible interactions not fully understood
Incremental aspects: heavy adaptation of TetraJet [22] primarily switching MXFP4→NVFP4; while LLM application is novel, some contributions extend rather than replace prior art
Limited baseline comparisons: only compares to Quartet and NVIDIA's method; missing comparisons to recent FP4 methods like QuaRot [13]; NVIDIA baseline may not be fully open limiting reproducibility

Reproducibility concerns: code release not committed, custom NVFP4 kernels would be needed, stochastic rounding randomness handling unclear, hyperparameter selection justification minimal with no systematic search documented

Missing robustness analysis: no sensitivity studies for hyperparameter deviations, failure modes if oscillation detection fails, or edge case behaviors; limited discussion of when method might struggle

strengths: Novel OsciReset algorithm that effectively addresses weight oscillation in 4-bit LLM training, representing the first method specifically designed for this problem in pre-training
Technically sound NVFP4 linear layer design with unbiased gradient estimation, improving upon NVIDIA's approach through better scaling and aligned forward/backward computation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations, multiple model sizes, downstream task validation, and actual CUDA kernel implementations demonstrating 1.67× speedup
Well-motivated problem identification: distinguishes between quantization error and optimization-induced failures, with clear empirical demonstration of oscillation phenomenon (Fig. 1)
Strong reproducibility through detailed hyperparameter documentation (Appendix B), algorithm specifications (Appendix C), and memory overhead analysis showing practical scalability
weaknesses: Limited model scale: evaluation only on models up to 370M parameters contradicts claims about training 'large language models'; unclear if methods generalize to >1B parameter models or actual foundation models
Modest accuracy gains with 51.3% gap reduction leaving ~49% gap to BF16 (e.g., 370M val PPL 23.70→25.11); unclear if this accuracy loss is acceptable for production use cases
Evaluation restricted to single architecture (OLMo-2) with no validation on LLaMA, Mistral, or other widely-used LLMs, limiting generalizability claims in abstract and introduction

Heuristic design choices lack principled justification: OsciRisk metric formulation not compared to alternatives, bin-center reset not proven optimal, static outlier selection assumptions not systematically validated beyond Appendix C.3

Incomplete theoretical analysis: claim of 'practically optimal convergence' (abstract) relies on citation without formal proof for the specific configuration; no convergence rate analysis incorporating quantization + oscillation suppression effects

Missing critical analyses: no gradient dynamics comparisons with BF16, no investigation of oscillation severity vs. model size, FP6×FP4 precision switching experiment (Fig. 6) shows substantial gains but remains underdeveloped suggesting current FP4 approach may be fundamentally limited

Reproducibility gaps despite detailed hyperparameters: code availability promised but link omitted, hyperparameter tuning methodology not fully disclosed, random seeds and initialization details missing
Experimental design concern: NVIDIA baseline modified to full 4-bit (vs. original mixed-precision) for comparison fairness, potentially disadvantaging the baseline

strengths: Well-motivated identification of specific optimization challenges in low-precision training (weight oscillation and outliers) with clear visualizations and concrete examples
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablation studies across multiple dimensions, model sizes (70M-370M), and downstream tasks
Demonstrated practical speedups (1.67× over FP8) with efficient CUDA kernel implementations and detailed latency analysis
Generally well-written presentation with good use of figures, detailed appendices with reproducible hyperparameters, and robustness analysis for key hyperparameters
Addresses an important practical problem of making 4-bit training efficient for LLMs
weaknesses: Limited novelty: individual components are refinements of existing techniques (double-block quantization is straightforward, OutControl adapts known methods, OsciReset while novel is relatively simple), resulting in primarily an engineering contribution rather than algorithmic innovation

Weak theoretical justification for the main novel component (OsciReset): lack of principled analysis for why resetting to bin centers is optimal, absence of convergence guarantees, and insufficient explanation of the root cause of oscillation emerging specifically at end of training

Evaluation limited to small models (only up to 370M parameters) with single architecture family (OLMo-2), making generalizability unclear and raising concerns about scalability to truly large models where different optimization dynamics may emerge
Significant remaining gap to full precision despite improvements (5.9% relative gap in validation PPL for 370M model), with unclear practical acceptability for production applications
Artificial experimental setup: converting NVIDIA's intentionally mixed-precision recipe to fully 4-bit for comparison, making the fairness of comparison questionable

Outlier handling method (static selection based on early training statistics) lacks depth: limited analysis of why specific patterns are problematic, no ablation on the 10% selection threshold, and potential brittleness if activation patterns change during training

Missing comprehensive comparisons: recent baselines relegated to appendix, limited discussion of contemporary FP4 training work, and narrow hyperparameter sensitivity ranges (only ~50% variation from nominal values)

Insufficient analysis of key design choices: limited explanation for why RHT application differs from prior work, choice of resetting period (200 steps) appears ad-hoc, and exploration of FP6 variants suggests full FP4 may not be optimal target

strengths: Novel identification and characterization of weight oscillation as a key failure mode in FP4 LLM training, with clear empirical demonstration (Figure 1)
Well-motivated algorithmic solution (OsciReset) that elegantly addresses oscillation through weight resetting, with superior performance to prior Vision Transformer methods adapted to LLMs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple model scales, large token budgets, extensive ablations isolating individual components, and downstream task validation
Demonstrated practical efficiency gains through implemented CUDA kernels showing 1.67× end-to-end speedup over FP8 with detailed latency breakdowns for different configurations

Thorough analysis including loss decomposition (Tables 3-4) revealing bottlenecks, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis showing robustness, and principled investigation of oscillation-quantization error relationships
Strong reproducibility practices: detailed hyperparameter specifications, complete algorithms, promised code release, compatibility verification with different optimizers (Muon)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-structured appendices providing implementation details for both naive and memory-efficient variants
Unbiased gradient estimation through careful design choices (stochastic rounding, proper tensor alignment) with theoretical justification from prior convergence guarantees
weaknesses: Significant limitation in experimental scope: evaluation restricted to OLMo-2 models up to 370M parameters only; generalization to larger models (1B+, 7B, 13B) and other architectures (LLaMA, Qwen, Mistral) remains unvalidated, limiting practical impact claims for current LLM scales

Remaining performance gap to BF16 is material: OLMo-2-370M shows 25.11 vs 23.70 validation PPL gap (~1.4 points, larger than typical training variance); framing as '51.3% reduction' is relative to baselines, not absolute
Mixed-precision in best results contradicts 'fully 4-bit' framing: TetraJet-v2-full retains 10% of activations in FP8, technically requiring dual precision support on hardware

Complex hyperparameter set (τ_osci, T_start, T_period, T_accu, outlier selection ratio p) with limited generalization validation; sensitivity analysis only on OLMo-2-150M raises concerns about transferability

Significant theoretical gaps in design justification: bin-center reset choice appears empirically determined rather than principled; 1×128 outer block size and 10% outlier threshold lack principled derivation and may not generalize to other quantization formats
Overhead analysis limitations: measured only on specific 8×RTX5090 configuration; scaling to different hardware platforms, batch sizes, and distributed training strategies unclear
Hardware/timeline specificity: evaluation on RTX 5090/6000 Pro for relatively new NVFP4 format; applicability to other accelerators and adoption timeline uncertain

Limited statistical rigor: no error bars or confidence intervals, single runs per configuration (understandable for large-scale training but worth noting), downstream evaluations without variance estimates
